<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:rna}
The strong Rost Nilpotence holds for Artin-Tate motives.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Indeed, 
for any $\psi\in \operatorname{End} (M)$, we have $\psi=\psi_1\oplus\ldots \oplus\psi_r$, where each $\psi_i\in \operatorname{End}(M_i)$. Hence, we may assume $M$ is the motive of some 0-dimensional variety $X$. But the restriction morphism $res_{l/k}$ is known to be injective in this case (the Chow group of $X$ is free).
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
The strong Rost Nilpotence holds for the motive $\operatorname{M}(Y)$.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{generic}
Let $X$ be an irreducible smooth projective variety over $k$. Assume that $X$ satisfies the strong Rost nilpotence generically (that is the $k(X)$-variety $X_{k(X)}$ satisfies the strong Rost nilpotence). 
Then $X$ satisfies the strong Rost nilpotence.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Following the proof of \cite[Prop.3.1]{VZ08} the restriction morphism  factors as the composite
\[
\operatorname{End}_k(\operatorname{M}(X))\xrightarrow{res_{X/k}} \operatorname{End}_{X}(\operatorname{M}(X_X))\xrightarrow{res_{k(X)/X}}\operatorname{End}_{k(X)}(\operatorname{M}(X_{k(X)}))
\]
where the middle term denotes endomorphisms in the category of Chow motives over the relative base $X$, the first map is injective, and the second map is induced by passing to the generic point of $X$. 
Observe that the kernel of $res_{k(X)/X}$ is the nilpotent ideal by the proof of \cite[Lem.3.2]{VZ08} extended in \cite[\S3.5]{Gi25}. 

Now the kernel of the restriction $res_{l/k}\colon \operatorname{End}_k(\operatorname{M}(X)) \to \operatorname{End}_l(\operatorname{M}(X_l))$ is contained in the kernel of $res_{F/k}$, where $F$ contains both $l$ and $k(X)$, so is nilpotent.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
The strong Rost nilpotence holds for the motive $\operatorname{M}(Y_A)$.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
From \cite[\S2]{XZ24} it follows that the motive $\operatorname{M}(Y_A)$ splits as
\[
\operatorname{M}(Y_A)=N\oplus \bigoplus_{i=0}^{n-3}\operatorname{M}(\operatorname{SB}(A))(i),
\] 
where the motive $N$ is supported only in the middle codimension (over the algebraic closure of $k$, $N$ splits as a direct sum of Tate motives twisted by $n-2$).

Since $\operatorname{M}(Y_A)$ is supported in dimension zero only by the motive of a Severi-Brauer variety $\operatorname{M}(\operatorname{SB}(A))$, the latter must contain a Tate motive (in dimension 0) over the generic point $k(Y_A)$. Therefore, by \cite{Ka96} the algebra $A$ splits over $k(Y_A)$. Hence the variety $Y_A$ turns over $k(Y_A)$ into the variety $Y$, and the strong Rost Nilpotence holds for $Y_A$ generically. To finish we apply Lemma~\ref{generic}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
The canonical $p$-dimension of the variety $Y_A$  is equal to $d-1$.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $U$ be the upper motive of $\operatorname{M}(Y_A; \mathbb{F}_p)$. It is isomorphic to the indecomposable motive $\operatorname{M}(\operatorname{SB}(D_p);\mathbb{F}_p)$ up to a shift. Observe that $\dim(\operatorname{SB}(D_p))=d-1$. Being an indecomposable lower summand, the dual motive $U^*$ of $U$ is isomorphic to $U(\dim(Y_A)-d-1)$ by the Krull-Schmidt property (see \cite[Prop.5.2]{Ka10}). By \cite[Thm.5.1]{Ka10}, the canonical $p$-dimension of $Y_A$ is then equal to the dimension of $U$ that is $d-1$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
